description: A connected suite of five skills for building fictional worlds: gradual development, world systems and simulation, living canon, constructed languages, and evidence-first research. All five share one record vocabulary, so output from one imports cleanly into the others.

skills.name: gradual-worldbuilding
skills.description: The pace-and-method layer: develop worlds in earned layers instead of rushing toward an empire, endpoint, or encyclopedia. Governs sequencing, stage-gates, development ladders, and measurable capacity thresholds, and hands each increment off to the other skills in their own record formats.

skills.name: storycraft-os
skills.description: Build, simulate, govern, audit, and publish fictional worlds as durable causal systems: factions, cultures, religions, economies, ecology, geography, infrastructure, technology or magic systems, timelines, maps, campaigns, and persistent world state.

skills.name: living-canon-os
skills.description: Build, maintain, recall, audit, branch, and hand off durable living knowledge bases with transaction-governed canon changes and grounded retrieval: world bibles, lore and canon systems, campaign or series state, and continuity memory.

skills.name: conlang-design
skills.description: Design, expand, document, audit, test, translate, or evolve constructed languages as coherent, versioned communicative systems: phonology, phonotactics, grammar, lexicon, scripts, diachrony, corpus work, and interlinear glossing.

skills.name: worldbuilding-research
skills.description: Evidence-first research for worldbuilding: structured specs, batched source collection, and source records with calibrated confidence claims, producing research that imports into the other skills without reformatting.
